To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EOMCCSD(T) method is more accurate for 55Ni than the CI(4p-4) method and that the EOM(2,3)SD(T) method, which is computationally more demanding than the CI(3p-3) method, is more accurate than the CI(2p-2) method.

the EOMCCSDT and EOMCCSD(T) methods are accurate enough to be used for studying the structure of odd-mass nuclei with up to about 50 correlated particles, and that they can be applied to nuclei with up to 60 or so correlated fermions, provided that the reference state is sufficiently accurate.
the EOMCCSDTQ approach is accurate for the odd-A nuclei in the pf shell and that the EOM-CCSD(T) and EOMCCSD approaches can be used for the odd-A and even-even isotopes in the sd shell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of new methods of electronic structure theory and their application to problems in nuclear physics.
the practical implementation of the CC and CI methods for odd-A heavy nuclear systems, and we show that the CC methods can provide a reliable and accurate description of nuclear structure phenomena

the accuracy of the EOMCC methods with up to two-particle-two-hole (2p-2 h) components in the cluster and excitation operators, which are computationally less demanding than the full configuration interaction (CI) approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EOMCCSD(2,3) method with 2p-3h components in the excitation operator and 1p-2h and 2p-1h components in the correlation operator is a very accurate method that can be applied in practice to systems with 12 or fewer fermions in the valence space.
the EOMCCSD(2) approach with 2p-3h/3h components in the excitation operator is a very good choice for odd-mass nuclei.
the EOMCCSD(2,3) method is a very good choice for the description of odd-A nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CC methods are very promising for the pf-shell nuclei.
the CC methods with 2p-3h/2h-3p excitations in the EOM excitation operator can be considered as an optimal compromise between accuracy and efficiency for odd-A nuclei.
the EOMCCSDTQ(3p3h) approach with 3p- and 3h- excitations in both the cluster and EOM operators is the most accurate and efficient method for odd-A heavy nuclear structure calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EOMCC methods are more accurate than their CI counterparts for a given level of computational effort.

the EOMCCSD(3p-2) method, which is the most computationally efficient EOMCC approximation that can be applied in the pf-shell model space, is a viable alternative to the full CI approach for systems as large as 57Ni.
, in the pf-shell, the EOMCCSDT-1 approximation is as accurate as the EOMCC3 approach.
